## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-anonymized: "Neither author nor reviewers know the identity of each other"; the aim is at least two external reviewers per manuscript sent out (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/peer-review-information/review-process; retrieved 2026-11-23). Authors submit an anonymous file with acknowledgments and self-identifying links removed and self-citations in the third person (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/author-instructions/submitting-your-materials) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Yes. Authors rejected with reviews may transfer manuscript and anonymized reviews to a participating journal within 4 weeks; the page lists 33 participating journals (counted on the page 2026-11-23), among them International Organization, International Studies Quarterly, Journal of Conflict Resolution, Perspectives on Politics, Political Behavior, Political Analysis and Comparative Politics. Transfers in from other journals are accepted (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/peer-review-information/review-process) |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Not as standard practice per anything read. The 2024 editors' statement says they hope to offer published reviews and post-publication commentary alongside articles; no page read confirms that this has been introduced (Notes from the Editors, https://doi.org/10.1017/S0003055424001047) |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | SciRev, n = 12: 1.1 rounds on average (https://scirev.org/journal/american-political-science-review/, 2026-11-23). The incoming editors say they will end review after one round where the outcome is fairly clear and will not let a single reviewer veto (Notes from the Editors) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Authors may "oppose" a potential reviewer with specific reasons; the instructions discourage authors from naming people as potential reviewers (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/author-instructions/submitting-your-materials and .../preparing-your-materials, 2026-11-23). Authors are expected to review for the journal in turn; the editors may desk-reject authors who repeatedly fail to provide invited reviews (review-process page). Appeals of post-review rejections are allowed within 60 days after a 14-day cooling-off period; desk rejections cannot be appealed (same page) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes, a dedicated "Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Tools" section in the author instructions (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials; retrieved 2026-11-23), written "in accordance with" the Cambridge University Press research publishing ethics guidelines |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found. Use is allowed with declaration |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with a mandatory declaration for generative use; same rubric as the Mind entry) |
| **Summary** | AI tools cannot be listed as authors. Declare and describe any use of an AI tool to generate text or images (translation included) or to analyse or extract insights from data. Minimal non-generative uses (spelling or language checking, single words or brief phrases, minor formatting) need no declaration. Declaration goes in an acknowledgments section or footnote (text), in the methods section (data analysis) or in figure captions (images), and should give tool name and version, dates of use, how it was used and any citations to third-party material. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials |

## Format

> Source for the rules below: the journal's "Preparing your materials" and "Submitting your materials" pages under https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/author-instructions/ (retrieved 2026-11-23).

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Five types: Research Article, Research Note, Registered Report, Synthesis and Replication/Reappraisal (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/instructions-contributors). The Letter category was dropped in 2024 (Notes from the Editors, https://doi.org/10.1017/S0003055424001047). Book reviews, policy papers, special issues and papers about current events are not published (preparing-your-materials page) |
| **Word limit** | "No strict word limit": completed articles are expected to run below 11,000 words and research notes below 7,000; word counts exclude reference lists and supplementary material but include tables, figures and footnotes, and a word count must appear on the front page (preparing-your-materials page) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | The limit is worded as an expectation; the editors say the former limits were relaxed so that papers needing more space (they name qualitative or mixed-methods work) are easier to place (Notes from the Editors). No exception procedure is described |
| **Abstract limit** | 150 words or fewer (preparing-your-materials page). Median abstract length in the 660 Crossref records that have one: 148 words, maximum 207 (computed 2026-11-23) |
| **Reference limit** | No cap found; references are excluded from the word count (preparing-your-materials page). Author-date system of the Chicago Manual of Style, 17th edition; in-text format (Author Year, Pages); authors' full first and last names in the list; a link for every unpublished source |
| **Supplementary material** | Appendices and other material may be uploaded for reviewers and published online; appendices intended for print are to be distinguished from online ones (submitting-your-materials page). Quantitative replication data and code go to the APSR Dataverse after conditional acceptance (research-transparency page, https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/journal-policies/research-transparency) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Figures should read in grayscale; place figures and tables in the text or use a placeholder; tables of studies are suggested for three or more studies (preparing-your-materials page). Colour charges apply for print colour (fees-and-pricing page) |
| **Style / submission format** | Initial submissions need not follow the journal's stylistic requirements (they are applied before external review or at conditional acceptance). Stated style: 12-point font, double-spaced main text, page numbers, footnotes not endnotes; anonymous file without acknowledgments; Editorial Manager submission; ORCID required for corresponding authors; optional Overleaf template (preparing-your-materials and submitting-your-materials pages). The instructions ask authors to bring the main argument, the evidence and the findings into the introduction |

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

> Evidence layers: OpenAlex grouped counts over 756 works dated 2021-2026; Crossref records (766, 660 with abstract) for keyword counts; the incoming editors' published statement (https://doi.org/10.1017/S0003055424001047) and the outgoing team's report (Fall 2024 executive summary, URL in Metrics). Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Author countries on the 756 works dated 2021-2026 (OpenAlex; works with at least one author in the country): United States 483 (63.9%), United Kingdom 109, Germany 32, Canada 27, Denmark 27, Switzerland 18, Norway 17, Sweden 17, Italy 15, Spain 14, Netherlands 14, Israel 11 (retrieved 2026-11-23). The incoming editors write that they welcome all subfields, topics, methods and regions, "especially those traditionally under-represented", and judge articles by "what can be learned" rather than by site (Notes from the Editors). The counts show where authors are based, not where acceptance is easier |
| **Editorial-board geography** | 155 entries on the live page (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/editorial-board, retrieved 2026-11-23), recounted by the country printed after each name: United States 135, United Kingdom 9, Canada 3, Germany 2, and one each in France, Taiwan, Norway, Italy, Switzerland and Japan (135+9+3+2+6 = 155). The page text lists the 133-name editorial-board block twice; it was counted once |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Keyword counts in the 660 records with abstracts: colonial or Indigenous terms 37 (5.6%); China, Chinese, Taiwan or Hong Kong 14 (2.1%); Israel, Palestine or Gaza 4 (0.6%). The outgoing editors report their largest increases in accepted articles using qualitative case studies, critical or poststructuralist approaches and ethnography (Fall 2024 executive summary). The incoming editors' stated welcome for non-Western sites is in the first row |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Gender, women or feminism terms 78 (11.8%); race, racial, ethnic or minority terms 105 (15.9%); LGBT, queer, transgender or same-sex terms 11 (1.7%). The outgoing team states it pursued "representational" diversity and reports that race, ethnicity and politics had the largest share of accepted articles among the four most recent teams (Fall 2024 executive summary). The instructions' scope text says the journal aims to represent the diversity of subfields, areas, identities, methods and approaches (instructions-contributors page) |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | No single tradition is stated: the journal's text says contributions may be "empirical, interpretive, or theoretical" (preparing-your-materials page). By keyword counts in 660 records, experimental, survey and causal-identification designs lead, normative or political-theory terms come next (61, 9.2%), interpretive, hermeneutic, genealogical or poststructural terms are rare (9, 1.4%). The five most-cited 2021-2026 items in Crossref (citation counts at retrieval) are: fake news and partisan polarization (390; https://doi.org/10.1017/s0003055421000290), opinion effects of protest against police violence (309; https://doi.org/10.1017/s0003055421000460), repeated-measures survey designs (197; https://doi.org/10.1017/s0003055421000241), gendered political socialization of girls (172; https://doi.org/10.1017/s0003055421001027), and deindustrialization and voter backlash (169; https://doi.org/10.1017/s0003055421000022). The journal states no political position on any page read |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, a stated scope test: authors "must demonstrate how their analysis illuminates or answers an important research question of general interest in political science" (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials, retrieved 2026-11-23). Work "with a narrower focus usually fits more comfortably into subfield journals" (same page).
- **What kind of engagement?** A general theory or question, or an event of broad significance; regional or period studies should state their relevance to theory and politics elsewhere; political theory submissions should state relevance to the wider discipline or contemporary issues (same page). The page also asks for scope conditions and generalizability on empirical claims, and for formal models to state assumptions and empirical implications.
- **Article types and length**: five types (Research Article, Research Note, Registered Report, Synthesis, Replication/Reappraisal), articles expected below 11,000 words and notes below 7,000, abstract at most 150 words (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/instructions-contributors and the preparing-your-materials page, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **Scope exclusions**: no policy-advocacy papers, no papers about current events unless connected to a larger theory, no book reviews or special issues; papers that fit adjacent fields better are generally not reviewed; papers previously rejected are not reviewed again unless the empirics or theory are entirely new or resubmission was invited (preparing-your-materials page).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: the review-process page says editors return submissions without review when judged inappropriate or unlikely to survive review, and that roughly two-thirds of submissions are not sent out (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/peer-review-information/review-process, retrieved 2026-11-23). It does not say which share of desk rejections is for scope.

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are Crossref records of this journal dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 (766 journal-article records; 660 with an abstract) whose title or abstract matches the regex listed under AI-Research Notes. Shares use 660 as the denominator. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; a 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. No 4-5 is assigned: the journal's editorial text welcomes a range of methods without ranking them (Notes from the Editors, https://doi.org/10.1017/S0003055424001047; preparing-your-materials page). Rows for political-science practice are added where the schema's rows do not fit; the schema rows are kept and marked where they do not apply.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | Experiment, randomized, field-experiment or survey-experiment terms 149 (22.6%) of 660 (regex `experiment`). The instructions say preregistration is "generally expected for experiments" and that quantitative replication materials are verified after conditional acceptance (preparing-your-materials and research-transparency pages) |
| Quantitative observational / causal inference (added row) | 3 | Causal-identification terms 102 (15.5%) (regex `causal_identification`); survey, panel-data, cross-national or public-opinion terms 172 (26.1%) (regex `survey_data`) |
| Qualitative interviews | 3 | `interviews?` 34 (5.2%), the word "qualitative" 31 (4.7%) of 660; the score sits at the 5% boundary. The incoming editors say relaxed length limits should make it easier for qualitative or mixed-methods work (Notes from the Editors) |
| Qualitative case studies (added row) | 2 | Case-study, process-tracing, comparative-historical or within-case terms 19 (2.9%) (regex `case_study`). The outgoing team reported its largest increase among accepted articles was in qualitative case studies, critical or poststructuralist approaches and ethnography, without counts in the summary (Fall 2024 executive summary) |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Does not fit political science as a named method: 0 of 660 records match `auto-?ethnograph`; ethnography generally matches 4 (0.6%). The row is kept for schema parity |
| Theoretical / Conceptual (normative theory) | 3 | Normative, political-theory, political-philosophy, democratic-theory or theories-of-justice terms 61 (9.2%) (regex `normative_theory`). Political theory is one of the subfields the journal names (about-this-journal page) |
| Formal theory (added row) | 2 | Formal-model, formal-theory, game-theory, equilibrium, signaling-game, bargaining-model or theoretical-model terms 14 (2.1%) (regex `formal_model`; narrow, so a lower bound). The instructions say papers with formal claims should include complete proofs, reviewed at the conditional-acceptance stage, and that a formal model need not be tested with data (preparing-your-materials page; Notes from the Editors) |
| Mixed methods | 2 | Mixed-methods, multimethod or nested-analysis terms 7 (1.1%) (regex `mixed_methods`) |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 1 | Meta-analysis or systematic-review terms 5 (0.8%) of 660 (regex `meta_sr_only`). Note: the journal lists "Synthesis" (summarizing a field, usually with some empirical analysis such as meta-analysis) as one of its five article types (instructions-contributors page), and replication, reappraisal or registered-report terms are in 9 records (1.4%, regex `meta_replication`); the score follows the count rule and is not raised for that |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Of the 660 Crossref records with an abstract (2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23), 588 (89.1%) contain I, we, my or our (case-sensitive regex `\b(?:I|we|my|our|We|My|Our)\b`, applied to abstract text only; an independent recount on title plus abstract gave 589; retrieved 2026-11-23). The ten most recently published records with abstracts (dated 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-19, e.g. https://doi.org/10.1017/s000305542610224x, https://doi.org/10.1017/s0003055426102226, https://doi.org/10.1017/s0003055426101993) include nine with first person. The instructions state no first-person rule |
| **Expected density** | Articles below about 11,000 words including footnotes, tables and figures but excluding references; notes below 7,000 (preparing-your-materials page, retrieved 2026-11-23). Abstracts at most 150 words; median 148 in the Crossref sample |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Abstract of 150 words or fewer (preparing-your-materials page). No keyword count or requirement was found on the pages read |
| **Writing style notes** | Authors "must strive to be understandable to as many scholars as possible", should state the main argument, evidence and findings in the introduction, keep literature reviews brief and avoid straw men, and may use a table to summarize studies or prior work; author-date Chicago style; footnotes not endnotes; acronyms and computational abbreviations for variables discouraged (preparing-your-materials page, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Authorship pattern** | Crossref author lists for 693 of the 766 records: 1 author 275 (39.7%), 2 authors 194, 3 authors 134, 4 or more 90 (275+194+134+90 = 693). Retrieved 2026-11-23 |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages and the editors' own reports show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | The board page lists the sub-teams and affiliations but not disciplines or methods, so no methodological split can be counted. Structure (live page, retrieved 2026-11-23): 2 lead editors, 14 associate editors, 133 editorial-board members, 1 managing editor, 5 members of an Advisory Board for Ethical Research (2+14+133+1+5 = 155). The incoming team is "sixteen editors at thirteen different universities" (Notes from the Editors) | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/editorial-board ; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0003055424001047 |
| **Reviewer list size** | No separate reviewer list found on the pages read. The review-process page says the aim is at least two external reviewers and the incoming editors seek a minimum of two rather than three (SciRev average over 12 reviews: 3.0 reports) | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/peer-review-information/review-process ; https://scirev.org/journal/american-political-science-review/ |
| **Review model** | Double-anonymized (review-process page). The incoming editors say they will not let an individual reviewer veto and will override negative reviews where they see a compelling justification for publication (Notes from the Editors) | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/peer-review-information/review-process ; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0003055424001047 |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Blank. No first-hand report of reviewer competence was found: SciRev prints difficulty of reviewer comments 5.0 of 5.0 and quality of review reports 3.5 of 5.0 for n = 12 reviews, which is a rating, not a description of variance | https://scirev.org/journal/american-political-science-review/ |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Blank. No source describes reviewer treatment. Context only: quantitative designs dominate the published records (experiment, survey and causal terms in 22.6%, 26.1% and 15.5% of 660 abstracts) while the editors state a welcome for qualitative and mixed-methods work | OpenAlex and Crossref counts, see Methodological Preferences; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0003055424001047 |
| **Discourse community signals (author side)** | Board by country: United States 135 of 155 entries; author side: United States on 483 of 756 works (63.9%), United Kingdom 109 (OpenAlex, 2021-2026) | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/editorial-board ; OpenAlex works API, retrieved 2026-11-23 |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | All authors answer an ethics screening in the submission form. Papers with human participants (even if exempt from ethics review) must discuss consent, deception, confidentiality, harm, impact and compensation, confirm compliance with APSA's Principles and Guidance for Human Subjects Research or justify deviations, and declare funders (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials, retrieved 2026-11-23). An Advisory Board for Ethical Research of 5 members is listed on the board page |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author records are 275 of 693 Crossref records with author lists (39.7%) for 2021-2026 (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank. The pages read do not state an affiliation rule: the instructions, submission page and about page were searched for "independent scholar", "unaffiliated" and similar terms with no match (2026-11-23); no reviewer or board list gives affiliations by type |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Required. Quantitative reproduction materials and process documentation go to the APSR Dataverse; where data cannot be shared, authors must explain why and still share code and a way to obtain the data; accepted papers are checked for reproducibility and formal claims for consistency (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/journal-policies/research-transparency, retrieved 2026-11-23). Preregistration is "generally expected" for experiments, with signposting of registered and unregistered analyses (preparing-your-materials page) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-anonymized with an anonymous manuscript file; acknowledgments, author-identifying links and redacted self-citations are not allowed (third-person self-citation required) (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/author-instructions/submitting-your-materials, retrieved 2026-11-23). Preprints may be posted at any time (open-access-options page), which can reveal an author's identity |
| **AI use** | Declaration required for generative use that produces text or images or analyses data; AI cannot be an author (preparing-your-materials page, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; Gold OA APC GBP 2,610 or USD 3,655; many institutional agreements cover it (fees-and-pricing and open-access-options pages, retrieved 2026-11-23). Non-OA route: no submission fee was found on the pages read |
| **Reviewing obligation** | Authors are expected to review for the journal in turn; authors who repeatedly fail to provide invited reviews may be desk-rejected, and the incoming editors say they may refuse submissions from authors who decline two reviews when clearly qualified (review-process page; Notes from the Editors) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: papers must show a research question of general interest to political science; narrower work is steered to subfield journals; policy-advocacy and current-events papers, book reviews and special issues are not published (Framing Requirements; preparing-your-materials page).
- **Anonymity**: the submission must be an anonymous file without acknowledgments or identifying links, with self-citations in the third person (Peer Review; submitting-your-materials page). Manuscripts with compromised anonymity may be returned.
- **Data and code**: quantitative reproduction materials must be deposited in the APSR Dataverse after conditional acceptance, with an explanation if data cannot be shared (Data transparency requirement; research-transparency page).
- **Reference accuracy**: a reference that corresponds to no published work leads to desk rejection without resubmission (preparing-your-materials page, "References").
- **Prior rejection**: a previously rejected paper is not reviewed again unless resubmission was invited or the empirics or theory are entirely new (preparing-your-materials page).
- **AI use**: undeclared generative use for text, images or data analysis breaches the journal's AI section (AI Policy).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: no reported turnaround exists for the current team; the outgoing team's medians were 10 days to desk reject and 77 to 91 days after peer review, and SciRev (n = 12) lists 6.3 months for accepted manuscripts (Review Cycle Time).
- **Selectivity**: about 6% accepted, 1,700 or more submissions expected in 2024, and two-thirds not sent to review on the journal page (Metrics, Desk Rejection Rate). Only the odds of reaching review, not review outcomes, are covered by the figures.
- **Cost**: the Gold OA APC is GBP 2,610 or USD 3,655 unless an institutional agreement applies (Open Access).
- **Reviewing**: authors are expected to review for the journal and repeated failures may lead to desk rejection (Peer Review, Practical Concerns).
- **Preprints and anonymity**: preprints are allowed at any time but can reveal authorship under double-anonymized review (Preprint Policy, Practical Concerns).

### Best Suited For

- Empirical work with an identification or experimental design and a general question: experiment, survey and causal terms in 22.6%, 26.1% and 15.5% of 660 abstracts; the five most-cited 2021-2026 items are experimental or survey studies (Methodological Preferences; Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Political theory and formal theory with wide relevance: normative or theory terms in 9.2% of abstracts and formal-model terms in 2.1%; the journal names political theory among its subfields and accepts proofs-based work (Methodological Preferences; about-this-journal page).
- Qualitative and mixed-methods work that needs room: editors say they relaxed limits for it and the outgoing team reports growth in qualitative case studies and ethnography (Format; Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Replications, registered reports and syntheses: they are named article types (Format; instructions-contributors page).

### Not Recommended For

- Single-region or single-issue work with no wider theoretical claim: the instructions say narrower work fits subfield journals (Framing Requirements).
- Policy-advocacy papers, commentary on current events, book reviews or special-issue proposals (Framing Requirements).
- Authors who cannot share data, code or ethics documentation: the journal requires them or a reasoned explanation (Practical Concerns).
- Authors needing a verified turnaround or acceptance probability for the current team before choosing: none is published (Review Cycle Time; Metrics).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The rows are journals the APSR review-process page lists as participating in review transfer (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-political-science-review/information/peer-review-information/review-process, counted 2026-11-23); no entry for them exists in this corpus yet, so they are named without links. The list says transfer is possible, not that they accept transferred papers.

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | Perspectives on Politics | Listed as a transfer participant; also an APSA-family journal (published on the same Cambridge subscription bundle per the about-this-journal page). No fit evidence collected here |
| 2 | International Studies Quarterly | Listed as a transfer participant. No fit evidence collected here |
| 3 | Political Behavior | Listed as a transfer participant. No fit evidence collected here |
